meta.title: Mentiko Security Review
meta.summary: Security triage hub for control-plane to tenant, tenant to control-plane, webhooks, terminal, scheduling, secrets, env, and dependency risk.

pages.title: control-plane and tenant security report
pages.summary: Explains why each finding matters, what is intentional for a dev platform, and what happens if it is not fixed.

features.title: tenant shell command injection
features.summary: Auth-only routes build shell strings from workspace paths, conversation ids, file paths, or task ids. A dev platform may run commands intentionally, but the command must be chosen by the product, not by shell metacharacters hidden in request data.
features.impact: Any authenticated tenant user who can reach these routes may execute unintended shell commands in the tenant runtime.
features.intentionalBoundary: Running approved dev commands is intended; shell injection through route parameters is not.

features.title: terminal sessions lack owner and workspace scope
features.summary: Terminal list, capture, input, and websocket attach paths prove a user exists but do not prove that user owns the session or workspace. A shared dev platform cannot treat every authenticated user as the same operator.
features.impact: One tenant user can inspect, capture, or steer another user session, including output that may contain tokens, code, prompts, credentials, and customer data.
features.intentionalBoundary: Collaborative terminals are intentional only with explicit sharing and audit state.

features.title: terminal spawn accepts arbitrary cwd and injects secrets
features.summary: The terminal spawn route accepts a caller-supplied cwd and injects profile, workspace, and org secrets into the PTY environment. Workspace membership exists elsewhere but is not enforced here.
features.impact: A user can start a shell outside the intended workspace and receive decrypted secrets in process env, making accidental or malicious exfiltration easy.
features.intentionalBoundary: Secrets in runtime env can be intentional for an agent job; they should be scoped, auditable, and bound to an authorized workspace.

features.title: profile resolved-env returns plaintext vault secrets
features.summary: The resolved-env endpoint resolves profile env vars and returns plaintext values to the browser after only checkAuth. That crosses the line from server-side secret use into user-visible secret disclosure.
features.impact: Any authenticated org user with a profile id can pull decrypted env values instead of only using them inside controlled execution.
features.intentionalBoundary: Previewing which secret keys are wired is okay; returning decrypted values is not.

features.title: platform imageTag reaches tenant-host shell
features.summary: Control-plane records platform build metadata and later passes image refs into tenant-host shell commands. Without a strict image allowlist and safe argument passing, release metadata becomes a deploy-time command or image substitution boundary.
features.impact: If build metadata or the release ingestion path is compromised, tenant hosts can pull an attacker image or execute injected shell content.
features.intentionalBoundary: Automated tenant deploys are intended; accepting unguarded image refs is not.

features.title: secretless webhook receivers can trigger chains
features.summary: External webhook subscriptions allow missing secrets. That can be okay for passive ingestion, but risky when the webhook can create events that launch agent chains.
features.impact: Anyone with the receiver URL can trigger work, spend tokens, run actions, or create noisy automations if that subscription launches chains.
features.intentionalBoundary: Public inbound webhooks are intentional only when their trigger capability is explicit and signed or tokened.

features.title: deploy key can create canary tenants
features.summary: The test-provision route accepts DEPLOY_API_KEY and can create or resume tenant provisioning. A deploy key should deploy, not mint billable infrastructure unless that is a separate canary-only contract.
features.impact: A leaked CI or mk deploy key can allocate compute, DNS, and storage without an admin browser session or Stripe-backed flow.
features.intentionalBoundary: Automated canary provisioning is fine with a distinct key and hard scope.

features.title: bootstrap and deploy flows expose operational secrets
features.summary: Callback secrets and GHCR tokens appear in bootstrap files, cron-style command surfaces, or SSH argv. Host-local exposure is not the same as internet exposure, but it widens blast radius after any tenant-host foothold.
features.impact: A low-privileged host read or process listing can reveal callback or registry credentials that should have stayed root-only or stdin-only.
features.intentionalBoundary: Bootstrap needs secrets briefly; it should not leave them in world-readable files or process arguments.

features.title: plain secrets API is auth-only for write and delete
features.summary: The plain /api/secrets route lists metadata and allows create, update, and delete after checkAuth. Newer secret routes already use stronger manage_org or secrets scopes, so this older route is behind the product boundary.
features.impact: A lower-role member can corrupt or remove secrets that future jobs and terminals depend on, even if plaintext values are not returned.
features.intentionalBoundary: Secret management is intentional for owners/admins, not every authenticated member.

features.title: prod dependency advisories are currently open
features.summary: Both tenant web and control-plane have production npm audit findings. These are not all equal, but Next.js, better-auth, ws, nodemailer, jspdf, mermaid, and transitive parser/server packages touch public or privileged surfaces.
features.impact: Known public advisories stay reachable in app-router, auth, websocket, PDF, email, and rendered-content paths until versions are bumped and tested.
features.intentionalBoundary: Using fast-moving web frameworks is intentional; shipping known vulnerable prod versions is not.

features.title: provisioning callback auth is mostly sound
features.summary: The callback path uses bearer plus HMAC by default, timestamp skew, timing-safe signature checks, body validation, and replay cache. The remaining action is to verify HMAC is not disabled in production.
features.impact: This is not a current reportable issue based on static trace.

features.title: schedule raw_exec is not the same bug
features.summary: The schedule raw_exec path requires manage_org and uses spawn with shell:false. It is powerful by design, but the checked path did not show shell injection as written.
features.impact: Keep it RBAC-gated and audited; do not weaken this pattern when fixing terminal and chain paths.
features.intentionalBoundary: This is the model the other execution paths should move toward.

commands.title: route auth coverage
commands.summary: node scripts/check-auth-coverage.mjs reports markers, not complete authorization quality.

rules.title: dev power is intentional only behind explicit boundaries
rules.body: Powerful actions are acceptable when role, workspace, session owner, audit trail, and secret scope are explicit. Bare checkAuth plus shell/env access is not enough.

decisions.reason: verify the webhook fix requires HMAC or receiver token for chain-triggering subscriptions.

actions.title: replace shell strings with arg arrays
actions.command: kdex context "fix tenant shell injection paths" --limit 8
actions.reason: highest likelihood path to tenant runtime compromise

actions.title: bind PTY sessions to owner workspace and org
actions.command: kdex context "fix terminal session owner and workspace authorization" --limit 8
actions.reason: prevents cross-user terminal capture and steering

actions.title: remove plaintext resolved-env response
actions.command: kdex context "remove plaintext profile resolved env endpoint" --limit 8
actions.reason: secret values should resolve server-side only

actions.title: plan and test production dependency bumps
actions.command: kdex context "plan mentiko and control-plane security dependency bumps" --limit 8
actions.reason: npm audit has production high and critical advisories

actions.title: refresh secretless webhook receivers can trigger chains
actions.command: kdex context "refresh docs for secretless webhook receivers can trigger chains using web/app/api/webhooks/route.ts, web/app/api/webhooks/[id]/receive/route.ts, lib/chain-event-watcher.sh" --limit 8 | claude -p "Update the KDEX docs section 'secretless webhook receivers can trigger chains'. Use these source files as evidence: web/app/api/webhooks/route.ts, web/app/api/webhooks/[id]/receive/route.ts, lib/chain-event-watcher.sh. Keep it human-readable, preserve source links, and rehash after human review."
actions.reason: verify the webhook fix requires HMAC or receiver token for chain-triggering subscriptions.
